outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial have solution_passed true. The concrete task-solving difference is process and delivery. Parallel used repeated multi-agent mapping/order delegation and was still working through remaining slugs in the final timed-out round, so the harness collected only 137 requirement_patches. Serial used a single parent path to sync the target tree and generate all 193 patch artifacts before official collection.
parallel_contributors: Repeated child fan-out and retry rounds consumed the available closure budget.
Final-round parent activity still showed remaining slug mapping and artifact work.
Official harness collection stopped at 137 patch artifacts.
serial_contributors: No delegation overhead or child-result lifecycle was present.
The parent confirmed all 193 patch files and a clean tree before local testing.
Official harness collection found all 193 patch artifacts.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial chose a broad target-tree synchronization strategy; parallel mostly used granular cherry-pick/backport queues.
Both final official test sets passed, so these differences do not explain an official pass/fail split.
evaluator_effects: The official solution_passed field remained true for both modes despite the parallel artifact-count shortfall.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; parallel adverse process consequence only
